book_title: Chapter 8: Reading the Tape — Trend, Volume & Momentum Opportunity
question: What does the November 23, 2026 multi-timeframe price and volume structure say about institutional accumulation vs. distribution, and why is new capital gated by CAP_REJECTED?

epigraph.quote: Never argue with the tape. A great company in a Stage 4 downtrend will still take your capital while it searches for a floor.
epigraph.author: Stan Weinstein, Secrets for Profiting in Bull and Bear Markets

Meanwhile, the November 23 NSE daily OHLCV ledger classifies Stage 3 (Topping / Pullback) with 7 distribution days over 25 sessions, Daily RSI(14) at 38.50 (TradingView 40.35), and 28-day relative strength plunging to -34.99% (down from -29.03% on Nov 13; 63-day RS -20.10%) [28].

web_blocks.title: CAP_REJECTED Rule: Zero New Capital Until a Stage 1 Base & Stage 2 Breakout Form
paragraphs: When a stock trades -7.50% below its 30-week SMA and -12.21% below a falling 50-day SMA with -34.99% 28-day relative strength and 7 distribution days, buying dips is catching a falling knife. New capital is REJECTED until APARINDS builds a multi-week Stage 1 base and reclaims the 30-week SMA (₹15,405.10) on institutional volume.

book_paragraphs: Every fundamental thesis must eventually answer to the scoreboard of supply and demand, and as of November 23, 2026, the tape on Apar Industries has grown decisively more hostile. While the company's factories and ₹15,025 Cr order book kept its business-quality rating at COMPOUNDER_PASS, the stock price is locked in a Weinstein Stage 4 markdown.

Look at the deterioration since our mid-November review. At ₹14,250 on TradingView (₹14,184 on the NSE daily OHLCV ledger), APARINDS has fallen 26.03% from its ₹19,265 peak. It now sits 12.21% below a falling 50-day moving average (₹16,232), 6.87% below its 10-week EMA (₹15,302), and 7.50% below its 30-week SMA (₹15,405). Relative strength has worsened further: 28-day RS plunged to -34.99% with 7 institutional distribution days on the ledger. Our TradingView scanner enforces a hard CAP_REJECTED ceiling.

Notice the one subtle tactical feature on the chart: price is resting directly on its rising 40-week EMA (₹14,235) and just 2.43% above its rising 200-day SMA (₹13,913), with daily RSI depressed at 40.35. That means the stock is stretched downward into a long-term moving-average shelf where short-term reflex bounces frequently occur—even though the 4-hour chart has not turned up yet. For fresh cash, that is not a buy signal; for an existing holder, it defines a disciplined bounce-exit window behind an upward-ratcheted hard stop at ₹13,178.14.

Let us zoom in on the exact anatomy of this Stage 4 breakdown so you can see why institutions are stepping back rather than stepping in. On the daily ledger through November 23, APARINDS logged 7 distribution days in 25 sessions—meaning heavy down-volume selling has repeatedly overpowered quiet rebound attempts. Over the last 28 trading days, relative strength against the Nifty 500 collapsed to -34.99%, worsening from -29.03% just ten days earlier, while 63-day relative strength slid to -20.10%. Even on November 25, when the stock ticked up +0.47% on TradingView to ₹14,250, session volume was only 101,915 shares against a 30-day average of 169,186 shares—a muted 0.60x volume ratio that signals weak short-covering rather than institutional accumulation.

Look overhead at the wall of trapped supply waiting for any rally. Every buyer who entered between September and early November is now underwater beneath three stacked moving averages: the falling 20-day SMA at ₹14,805.30 (-3.75% above price), the broken 10-week EMA at ₹15,301.76 (-6.87%), the 30-week SMA at ₹15,405.10 (-7.50%), and the heavy 50-day SMA at ₹16,231.54 (-12.21%). Meanwhile, on the 4-hour chart, the close sits beneath both the 4H 20-EMA (₹14,393.67) and the 4H 50-SMA (₹14,817.46), leaving intraday_4h_turn strictly false with 4H RSI at 44.65.

Step back and check the broader Indian market regime too. Nifty 500 breadth has contracted sharply from 72.1% in mid-November to just 55.2% of stocks above their 50-day moving average and 48.2% above their 200-day moving average, with 3 index distribution days. In narrow-breadth tape, capital concentrates tightly into confirmed Stage 2 leaders while Stage 4 laggards like APARINDS, Polycab, KEI, TARIL, and TD Power Systems bleed lower until a multi-week Stage 1 base absorbs the overhang.

book_callouts.title: NARRATOR'S REFLECTION
book_callouts.text: When APARINDS, Polycab, KEI, TARIL, and TD Power Systems are all in Stage 4 at the exact same time, the market is sending a sector-wide message. Respect the tape: never deploy fresh capital against institutional distribution.

book_subsections.title: Multi-Timeframe Anatomy (1W / 1D / 4H) & Why Volume Confirms Caution
paragraphs: Inspecting all three timeframes confirms why we refuse to catch this knife. On the weekly chart, APARINDS sliced cleanly beneath both the 10-week EMA (₹15,301.76) and the 30-week SMA (₹15,405.10), pulling weekly RSI down to 45.77. On the daily chart, every rally attempt has stalled below the falling 20-day SMA (₹14,805.30) and 50-day SMA (₹16,231.54), while November 23 volume fell to 101,915 shares—just 0.60x the 30-day average of 169,186.

On the 4-hour chart, the close of ₹14,250 sits beneath both the 4H 20-EMA (₹14,393.67) and the 4H 50-SMA (₹14,817.46), keeping intraday_4h_turn strictly false. Meanwhile, Nifty 500 breadth has contracted to 55.2% above the 50-DMA and 48.2% above the 200-DMA, meaning weak stocks are no longer being rescued by a rising tide.

book_subsections.title: Upward-Only Stop Ratchet & Cash-Equity Execution
paragraphs: Because APARINDS is not an NSE F&O stock, there is no liquid options chain for covered calls or protective puts. Risk management relies strictly on our upward-only stop-loss ratchet. Our prior dossier locked the structural stop at ₹13,127.14. With the live 200-day SMA rising to ₹13,912.61 and the scanner's invalidation floor stepping up to ₹13,178.14, we ratchet our hard stop upward by ₹51 to ₹13,178.14. We never lower a stop to accommodate a falling stock.

Notice also how wide daily volatility remains: ATR(14) stands at ₹650.39 (4.56% of share price) and Bollinger Band width sits at 19.07%. Because routine intraday swings exceed ₹600, placing a tight stop right at the 200-day SMA invites whipsaw. Anchoring the hard stop at ₹13,178.14—cleanly beneath both the 200-day SMA (₹13,912.61) and Classic Pivot S1 (₹13,503.33)—gives the stock room for an oversold reflex bounce toward ₹14,805–₹15,405 where we can exit methodically, while guaranteeing an immediate full exit if structural support fails.
